Fulton County Health Center used the resources generated through the 340B Drug Pricing Program to support access to comprehensive healthcare services for its rural community. In 2025, FCHC incurred approximately $1.07 million in uncompensated care costs and generated approximately $1.086 million in estimated 340B savings. 340B resources, together with other hospital resources, helped FCHC absorb uncompensated care and reimbursement shortfalls, maintain essential services that are not financially self-sustaining, including obstetric services, and expand community health services such as cardiac catheterization capabilities. Resources also help offset the financial impact of providing medically necessary care to patients covered by government-sponsored health plans when reimbursement does not fully cover the cost of care. These uses support FCHC's mission to maintain local access to care, serve patients regardless of ability to pay, and provide comprehensive services responsive to the needs of its rural community.
